steps.text: Whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt together in a medium bowl.

Beat sugar and butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes. Beat in egg, then stir in shredded zucchini. Gradually stir in flour mixture until incorporated. Mix in raisins. Cover dough and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight.
When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets.
Drop teaspoonfuls of chilled dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until set, 8 to 10 minutes, switching racks halfway through.
Remove from the oven. Allow cookies to cool slightly on the cookie sheets before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These moist zucchini cookies are tender and delicious cake-like cookies studded with chewy raisins and flavored with ground cinnamon and cloves.

review.reviewBody: Sooooo good. Stayed with recipe, only some substitutions: used butter instead of margarine and threw in some flax meal and used half whole wheat and half white flour. No cloves since I didn't have any. Guests ate them up. The lactating guest had four, and my children (2 and 4) loved them, raisins and all. For some reason, I didn't trust they were done at 10 minutes (convection oven). I left them in for 2 more, and some burned. Refridgerated overnight, the dough looked all lumpy with sharp points, but when baked, puffed up to these completely round dome-shaped muffin top-like cookies, no matter how sloppily I dropped the dough shapes. More of a cake texture than a drier cookie texture. Zucchini didn't show up at all in the finished cookie, but I used a food processor for the whole thing and dumped all ingredients in rather than sifting them in. What a time saver! Thanks for the great recipe.

Delicious! I did make some tweaks for my preference. Unsweetened applesauce for the butter, only 3 tb of coconut sugar, 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp cloves. I also used 1/2 c of pecans, 1/4 c dark chocolate chips, and a 1/4 c of semisweet chocolate chips.

I tweaked the recipe to fit my dietary needs. I used whole wheat flour, traded the sugar for 1/2 cup stevia and 1/2 cup brown sugar, added 1/4 cup of molasses and upped the baking soda to 1 1/2 tsp. They are delicious! I just made them yesterday and they are half gone! Everyone loves them.

Love this recipe! I deviated slightly and didnt have time to chill the dough. Instead I melted the butter and exchanged raisins for mini chocolate chips. The melted butter puffed the cookies right up and they are the perfect texture!

Refrigerating the dough overnight allowed the raisins so soak up the moisture from my undrained frozen grated zucchini. Even so, the dough was too wet and the cookies were flat so I had to add 1/4 c. more flour. Reduce the cloves to 1/4 tsp. Baked 10 min. on my air-bake cookie sheet. Be sure to grease the pan! I never had zucchini cookies before so it's nice to have another way to use them! Yield: 36 cookies.

I was never a fan of zucchini bread but after a few were given to us from a garden l decided to try something myself. Omg. Hands down amazing! I added a few things to this to make it my own. After overnight chill, I added maple syrup, vanilla and quick oats. Followed the rest of the instructions. They weren’t wet or mushy or spread out like some reviews so I’m not sure what happened there. These rose nicely and browned well.

Yum. These cookies were easy to make and taste delish. I added 1/2 tsp of nutmeg and replaced the margarine with butter. I also made sure to squeeze out as much water from the zucchini as possible. Will make again.

Super easy to make and tasty. I replaced raisins with chocolate chips (my grandson isn't too keen on raisins). I lined the cookie sheet with parchment paper that made cleanup a breeze and the cookies perfect. I baked the first batch for 8 minutes but it was a bit underdone. 10 minutes was just right. I think the chocolate chips made it a little too sweet, so I think the next time I'll try dried cranberries, or maybe reduce the sugar if using chocolate chips again.

We had an abundance of zucchini from the garden this year and this recipe was right on time. I did make some changes - used butter instead of margarine, 1/2 cup white sugar & 1/2 cup brown sugar instead of the 1 cup of white sugar, and zante currants instead of raisins. Incredible results - I can't stop eating them. Great recipe!
I used Stevia for the sugar and 3/4 cup of raisins for a great diabetic cookie.

I made some changes according to what I had in my cupboard. I used raw sugar and wholemeal SR flour, so I didn't need baking powder. I only had 1/2 zucchini so I also added 1 small carrot. I also added some vanilla extract and cocoa. The second batch I topped with flaked almonds before baking, and the third batch I topped with white chia seeds. YUM! My new favourite snack! Thanks for sharing!
I almost followed. Only 1/2 t soda. I do not like to taste it. I used 2 cups zuccini and I also added 1 c quick oatmeal a t Vanilla and these seem healthy and I think they kicked butt .
Followed the recipe exactly. Only added butterscotch chips. Tasty but more cake than cookie. Not suitable for travel.
Sooo good! Nice and soft.
This is fabulous just as is, husband loves it, and so do I. Great change from zuchini bread. Which I already have plenty of.
Delicious! Made mine in the food processor doubled the batch. Has to add some more moisture added applesauce. Next batch will have coconut too. Mabe some nuts.
Moist and easy. Perfect use for leftover zucchini.
This is my go to recipe for these cookies. So easy and delicious

I followed the recipe exactly and chilled the dough overnight in the fridge before baking. These turned out well, although the consistency is more like that of a muffin / cookie / traditional zucchini bread than a cookie. The flavor is really good if you like a spiced cookie with raisins. One suggestion: I would specify whether or not to drain the zucchini after grating, as some reviews seem to have done this but others did not (I was in the latter camp).
I doubled the zucchini & oops no cinnamon so I used apple pie spice & omitted the cloves. Super soft & yummy!
